reviewFindings.finding: The full-resolution printed radical bar ends at −x: the numerator is √(x³+x²−x)+2, with +2 outside the radical. On the original domain x≠−2, steps 1 and 2 are valid and give √(x³+x²−x)=x, necessarily x≥0. Squaring is a valid forward implication, but treating the squared equation as equivalent while omitting this sign restriction introduces an extraneous candidate. Its factorisation gives −1,0,1; the original fraction is 3 at −1 and 1 at both 0 and 1. Hence the actual solutions are 0 and 1 and the intended first loss of equivalence is Step 3, C, agreeing with the publisher. The previous B approval came from incorrectly reading +2 inside the radical; it is withdrawn and replaced by this exact-source derivation.
